title: As the 2026 midterms approach, economy is front and center
claim: Economy leads the open-ended congressional campaign agenda; many adults agree with neither party on AI.
uncertainty: Cross-section; does not establish an increase in electoral salience. | Open-ended responses are coded categories; cost-of-living is part of economy NET, not additive. | Adult party-agreement and registered-voter election-priority denominators differ. | National vote preference is not a House seat forecast.

title: Americans' evaluations of the economy remain negative
claim: Gasoline concern rose much more than other household-cost concerns between January and July; AI was not asked in January.
uncertainty: Since January, half the sample receives a combined gasoline/energy item and half receives separate gasoline/electricity items; use only the matching separate-item series. | Reported differences are percentage points, not statistical significance tests. | This is concern, not demonstrated voting priority or causal vote switching. | AI has no January baseline in this series.

title: U.S. Economic Confidence Improves in July
claim: Economic confidence recovered from May's trough; inflation as the nation's most important problem declined from May to July while immigration rebounded from June.
uncertainty: National problem priority is different from personal financial strain and election-specific issue priority. | July fieldwork ends July 19; later escalation is outside this survey. | Source provides earlier-wave values; current n and margin of error must not be assigned to every prior wave. | No causal attribution of confidence changes to the Iran conflict.

title: Affordability Dominates Americans' Financial Worries
claim: Energy costs became a more frequently named family financial problem than in April 2025; broad inflation remained the largest category.
uncertainty: Annual April-to-April comparison, not evidence about August momentum. | Family financial concern is not equivalent to voting intention. | Earlier-wave n must be obtained before a formal two-sample significance calculation.

title: New Marquette Law School Poll national survey finds inflation and cost of living the most important issue; economy next most important
claim: Opposition to the cost-benefit balance of data centers increased on a stable question; the current-issue list changed across waves and cannot support a clean salience trend.
uncertainty: Data-center attitude is not a measured share voting on data centers. | Current-issue choices added housing and the SAVE Act and removed the deficit in July; no clean trend from April Iran 24% to July 10%. The question asks current importance, not whether the issue determines the respondent's vote. | Party subgroups have larger uncertainty; no inferred individual cross-party coalition behavior. | AI bad-for-society July level equals April rather than showing a monotonic increase.

title: Marquette Law Poll finds Crowley leading Tiffany among likely voters, tied among all registered voters
claim: Data-center opposition is broad, but inflation dominates stated current-issue priorities. The gubernatorial result depends materially on the turnout screen.
uncertainty: October 2025 data-center wording mentioned a Microsoft cancellation; exclude it from the comparable baseline. | No conclusion that data-center opposition caused the governor preference gap. | Registered-voter and likely-voter results cannot be merged. | July-to-August changes of 1–2 points are not evidence of a statistically established change. | One state does not establish a national electoral trend. The issue-priority question asks current importance, not whether it determines the respondent's vote.

title: Young adults in the U.S. are increasingly wary of AI, concerned it will take jobs
claim: AI anxiety has risen more sharply among young adults than across adults overall; the concern concerns future employment, not observed job destruction.
uncertainty: June fieldwork was published in August; do not timestamp the opinion change as an August shock. | Youth opinion is not youth turnout or vote conversion. | Subgroup sample sizes and earlier fieldwork dates need retrieval before formal change tests. | A twenty-year expectation is not a forecast of 2027–2028 layoffs.

title: Poll: Costs Are the Top Health Care Issue for Voters in the Midterms, But Fraud Tops Republicans' List As Trump Administration Pushes Crackdown
claim: Health-cost priority and anti-fraud priority differ by party; concern about costs does not imply agreement on the financing response.
uncertainty: Within-health-policy priority differs from an all-issues most-important question. | Single comparable wave in this evidence packet; no claim of increasing salience. | Publication July 16; do not misdate to July 23.

title: PUCO orders AEP Ohio to create data center specific tariff
claim: PUCO ordered AEP Ohio to establish a separate data-center tariff intended to protect other customers from costs associated with data-center expansion.
uncertainty: Historical regulatory baseline, not evidence of a new 2026 policy or of voter salience. | An order to file a tariff is distinct from realized ratepayer savings. | This notice does not support assuming every Ohio utility uses identical terms.

title: Governor Mills Signs Executive Order to Establish Maine Data Center Advisory Council
claim: After a data-center moratorium bill was vetoed and the veto sustained, the governor created an advisory council with recommendations due January 29, 2027.
uncertainty: The advisory council is not a moratorium in force. | Governor supported a moratorium with a specified project exemption; do not code this as unconditional pro- or anti-data-center positioning. | Publication is evidence of an institutional response, not the cause of the response.

title: Executive Order 2026-05 – Protecting Pennsylvania Consumers from Data Center Impacts
claim: Executive Order 2026-05 differentiates new permit applications for data centers above 25 MW by GRID consent-agreement participation, removes data centers from Fast Track and directs advocacy for protective utility tariffs.
uncertainty: Sections 1(b)-(c) apply to new applications for projects above 25 MW. GRID participants receive rolling review but issuance waits for local approvals; nonparticipants face additional sequencing restrictions. This is not a moratorium or universal construction ban. | Section 3 directs counsel to advocate for PUC rules and tariffs concerning interconnection and reliability-backstop costs; the executive order does not itself establish those tariffs. Cost recovery remains subject to the appropriate regulatory process. | State action does not establish the policy of every state or federal preemption.

title: SB26-189 Automated Decision-Making Technology
claim: SB26-189 replaces the prior automated-decision framework; key duties cover consequential decisions, with major obligations beginning January 2027 and attorney-general enforcement.
uncertainty: Act effective May 14 is distinct from January 2027 obligations. | Do not apply unrevised SB24-205 assumptions. | Large roll-call majorities are recorded; party labels are not inferred from vote size. | Attorney-general rulemaking and specific company use cases affect compliance exposure.

title: President Donald J. Trump Unveils National AI Legislative Framework
claim: The administration proposes a uniform national AI framework, ratepayer protection, workforce measures and easier on-site-power permitting; the release explicitly seeks congressional legislation.
uncertainty: A requested national framework is not proof Congress enacted federal preemption. | Executive and legislative authorities must be analyzed separately. | Administration claims about benefits are policy intentions, not measured outcomes.

title: Medicaid Program; Community Engagement Requirement for Certain Individuals
claim: CMS implements a statutory community-engagement condition for applicable Medicaid beneficiaries from January 2027, subject to exceptions and possible good-faith state delays; outreach can precede the election.
uncertainty: Requirements apply to specified populations, not all Medicaid recipients. | Outreach date depends on state-selected review months. | Existing beneficiaries are assessed at the first renewal initiated after implementation; no assumption of immediate mass termination on January 1. | Governor or chamber turnover alone does not repeal the federal statute.

title: Fact Sheet: President Donald J. Trump Removes Regulatory Barriers to Affordable Home Construction
claim: A federal executive order directs agencies to review housing-related regulatory barriers, including water permitting and federal approvals.
uncertainty: Directions to review or revise rules are not delivered housing units. | Local land-use authority, implementation and financing conditions remain separate constraints. | This record makes no claim about the final status of H.R.6644 because search snapshots of that bill were inconsistent.

title: USTR Takes Action in Forced Labor Section 301 Investigations
claim: USTR announced final Section 301 tariffs of 10% or 12.5% on investigated economies, with differentiated treatment and product exemptions.
uncertainty: Headline tariff rates are not firm-level effective tariff rates; exemptions and MFN treatment matter. | Final action can still face litigation or amendment. | A changed Congress does not automatically reverse executive tariff administration.

title: Questions and Answers about the limitation on the deduction for business interest expense
claim: IRS's updated Section 163(j) guidance adds depreciation, amortization and depletion back to adjusted taxable income for tax years beginning after December 2024.
uncertainty: This is the applicable baseline, not a new prospective 2027 campaign promise. | Deduction limits, exceptions, elections and company taxable income determine cash benefits. | FAQs carry stated reliance limitations; this is investment-policy context, not personalized tax advice.

title: Federal Reserve issues FOMC statement
claim: FOMC held its target range at 3.50–3.75%; three dissenters preferred a quarter-point increase, while the statement described elevated inflation and energy supply shocks.
uncertainty: This is the July decision, not a prediction of September's decision. | An electoral affordability mandate does not directly set the federal funds rate.

title: Employment Situation News Release - August 2026
claim: August payroll employment rose 162,000 and unemployment held at 4.1% in the September 4 vintage.
uncertainty: Payroll figures are preliminary and subject to revision; preserve this release vintage. | Payroll and unemployment estimates come from different surveys. | No paid consensus forecast or surprise statistic is imputed.

title: Labor Force Characteristics of Foreign-born Workers - 2025
claim: Foreign-born workers represented 19.1% of the civilian labor force in 2025 and were disproportionately employed in several service, construction and production occupations.
uncertainty: Foreign-born is not synonymous with unauthorized or deportable. | 2025 annual estimates use eleven months because October CPS collection was interrupted; not a simple twelve-month average. | Regional occupational exposure is not an estimated causal effect of enforcement or immigration on election results.

title: The Budget and Economic Outlook: 2026 to 2036
claim: CBO's February baseline links fiscal support, tariff and immigration effects, and interest costs; it is a dated conditional baseline, not a September nowcast.
uncertainty: Does not incorporate later 2026 trade decisions or Iran developments. | Projected values are not realized facts. | Do not infer the post-midterm fiscal impulse from the total deficit; compare policy changes against an updated baseline.

title: Short-Term Energy Outlook - August 2026
claim: EIA's August outlook assumed severe Hormuz constraints through August with recovery beginning in September; its projected return toward pre-conflict production extended into early 2027.
uncertainty: A conditional agency forecast is not a verified probability that shipping normalizes on that schedule. | Distinguish financial prices, shipping flows, inventories and production. | Use the archived August PDF; a later September release lies outside the freeze.

title: 2026 Congressional Primary Dates and Candidate Filing Deadlines for Ballot Access
claim: The general-election calendar lists November 3, 2026 and state-specific nomination dates; New Hampshire's September 8 and later primaries were not complete at the freeze.
uncertainty: FEC compiles dates but state election offices administer elections. | Calendar is a May 18 vintage and dates can change; no assertion that every later modification is captured. | Do not use post-freeze New Hampshire primary results. | Louisiana timing can extend resolution beyond November 3.

title: Senate Facts - 119th Congress party lineup
claim: Senate Press Gallery's July 14 lineup is 53 Republicans, 45 Democrats and two independents caucusing with Democrats; its 2026 election list has 13 Democratic and 22 Republican seats.
uncertainty: The page labels a list Class II while including special-election seats; do not call all 35 seats regular Class II elections. | Race exposure differs by geography; national vote shares cannot translate mechanically into Senate control. | Dynamic site retrieved after freeze; use the dated lineup, not unrelated page updates.

title: NCSL State Elections 2026
claim: NCSL's June 25 summary identifies 6,139 legislative seats across 46 states and races in 88 of 99 state chambers.
uncertainty: Not every chamber elects all seats at once. | NCSL partisan-control color reflects party counts and may differ from governing coalitions. | This is an inventory, not a fitted 6,139-race prediction model.

title: Highlights from the 2026 NGA Summer Meeting
claim: NGA reports 39 gubernatorial elections scheduled for November, including territorial elections, with substantial turnover expected.
uncertainty: 39 includes territories; do not describe this as 39 U.S. states. | NGA's expectation of more than twenty new governors is a projection, not a final result. | Governor control does not imply control of both legislative chambers or independent regulators.

title: U.S. Senate: About Voting
claim: Most Senate passage votes require a simple majority; ordinary legislative cloture generally requires three-fifths of duly chosen and sworn senators; passage and cloture are distinct procedural thresholds.
uncertainty: Cloture and passage thresholds differ; specific exceptions and Senate precedents must be checked for each proposal. | Budget reconciliation is a constrained procedure, not a general bypass for all policy. | House/Senate control markets alone are not policy-enactment probabilities.

title: Notice of Election: Partisan Primary August 11, 2026 and General Election November 3, 2026
claim: The official county notice places Wisconsin's partisan primary on August 11 and general election on November 3; it lists January 4, 2027 as expiration of the current governor's term.
uncertainty: The statewide election dates are transferable; the listed legislative districts are county-specific and are not a statewide seat inventory. | An August 11 morning-to-September 8 price comparison crosses nomination resolution and first post-primary polling, so it cannot isolate an issue-salience effect. | Election timing is distinct from the assumption of office and from a policy's enactment or implementation date.

title: The Constitution of the United States: A Transcription
claim: The Constitution separates the president's four-year term, presidential presentment and veto, Senate consent to appointments, and the vice president's tie-breaking Senate vote; a congressional midterm result does not replace the presidency.
uncertainty: Holding the incumbent presidency fixed assumes ordinary continuation of the term; this is a scenario convention, not a statement that succession is impossible. | The vice president's floor vote does not itself specify committee organization or discharge arrangements in an evenly divided Senate. | An institutional route to policy is not a probability of enactment, an executive authority determination for a particular rule, or a forecast of Fed decisions.
